mainTopic: Changing how one carries on יום טוב, when we do not rebuke people, and starting to take from a storeroom (מוקצה)
overview: The amud opens with the last line of the משנה: on יום טוב one may start taking from a pile of straw, but not from wood in the storage yard. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying that if it is impossible to change the usual way of carrying, carrying normally is permitted. רבא puts this into practice in מחוזא with a ladder of changes, one for each kind of carrier. רב אשי then explains why women fill their water jugs normally on יום טוב: every possible change either adds work or risks a new איסור. Next, אביי explains why no one stops women from clapping and dancing on יום טוב: it is better that people sin without knowing than sin on purpose, and the גמרא adds that this applies even to Torah prohibitions. Finally, the גמרא brings two versions of רב כהנא's lesson about starting to take from a storeroom. In the first version the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who does not forbid מוקצה. In the second it follows רבי יהודה, and each version explains away the clause of the משנה that seems to go the other way.

steps.title: End of the משנה: straw pile allowed, storage wood not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying one may start taking from a pile of straw on יום טוב, but not from wood kept in the storage yard.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may begin taking from a pile of straw, but not from the wood in the storage yard.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It allows a person to start using a straw pile on יום טוב, but not wood that was put away in the back storage area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are set against each other. Straw in a pile may be started on יום טוב. Wood sitting in the מוקצה storage yard may not be started.

keyTerms.meaning: here: a storage yard behind the house where things are put away

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוקצה is the name of a place, a storage yard. It is not the general halachic category of objects set aside from use, even though the two are related.

phrases.english: from the pile of straw,
phrases.notes: The start of this sentence, "one may begin taking," comes just before this on the previous page.

phrases.english: but not from the wood in the storage yard.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲרֵמַת הַתֶּבֶן, אֲבָל לֹא בָּעֵצִים שֶׁבַּמּוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may begin taking from a straw pile, but not from wood in the storage yard.

steps.title: ברייתא: if you cannot change, it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: when it is impossible to change the usual way of doing something on יום טוב, one may do it normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that adds a limit to the משנה's rule about changing how one carries on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had required a person to change the weekday way of carrying things on יום טוב. This ברייתא adds that the requirement applies only when a change is possible. If it is not possible, carrying in the normal way is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion that explains the משנה
"it was taught", which introduces a ברייתא
to change, to do something differently from the weekday way

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for רבא's practical guidance in the next step, and he quotes it there word for word.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier part of the משנה about changing the way one carries things on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that limits the משנה's requirement to change.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When changing the usual manner is impossible, doing it the usual way is permitted.

steps.title: רבא's ladder of changes in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא set up a practice in מחוזא: each person moves one step up from his usual way of carrying, and if no change is possible, carrying normally is allowed, based on the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא instituted in מחוזא: Someone who carries with difficulty should carry on a pitchfork. Someone who carries on a pitchfork should carry on a carrying pole on the shoulders. Someone who carries on a carrying pole on the shoulders should carry it on a carrying pole in his hands. Someone who carries on a carrying pole in his hands should spread a scarf over it. And if that is not possible, it is permitted, as the Master said: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical set of rules for his city. Every type of carrier has a specific change he must make on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not to make carrying easier or harder. The point is to make it look different from a weekday. Each person's change depends on how he normally carries. רבא ends by bringing back the ברייתא from step 2: when no change is possible, normal carrying is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: instituted, set up a practice or rule
a carrying pole held on the shoulders by two people
a carrying pole held in the hands

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you change your usual way of carrying as much as you can. The kind of change depends on how you usually carry. If no change is possible, it is permitted.

phrases.english: Rava instituted in Mechoza:
One who carries with difficulty should carry on a pitchfork.
One who carries on a pitchfork should carry on a carrying pole on the shoulders.
One who carries on a carrying pole on the shoulders should carry it on a carrying pole in his hands.
One who carries on a carrying pole in his hands should spread a scarf over it,
and if it is not possible, it is permitted.
as the Master said:
phrases.notes: "The Master" here means the ברייתא quoted just above in step 2.

phrases.english: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the ברייתא into practice and quotes it as support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person must move one step away from his usual way of carrying on יום טוב. If no change is possible, carrying normally is allowed.

steps.title: Challenge: women fill water jugs without changing
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא asks רב אשי: the rule is to change as much as possible on יום טוב, so why do we say nothing to women who fill their jugs with water in the normal way?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said to רב אשי: The Rabbis said that as much as it is possible to change, we change on יום טוב. But these women fill their jugs with water on יום טוב without changing, and we say nothing at all to them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רבא points to a common sight that seems to go against the rule: women draw water on יום טוב in the usual way, and nobody tells them to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says to change whenever a change is possible. Filling a water jug could easily be done differently, yet everyone stays silent. This raises the question of why the rule is not enforced here. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said to Rav Ashi:
The Rabbis said: as much as it is possible to change,
we change on a Festival.
But these women

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מָלְיָין חַצְבַיְיהוּ מַיָּא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא,
phrases.english: who fill their jugs with water on a Festival,
and do not change,
and we do not say anything at all to them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָנֵי נְשֵׁי דְּקָא מָלְיָין חַצְבַיְיהוּ מַיָּא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of changing whenever possible, using a common practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that one must change as much as possible on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Filling water jugs could be done differently, yet women do it normally and no one objects. This seems to contradict the principle.

steps.title: No change is possible: switching jug sizes only makes it worse
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the women cannot change their way of filling water. A smaller jug means more trips, and a bigger jug means a heavier load.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: It is because a change is not possible. What should she do? If she usually fills a big jug, should she fill a small jug? Then she adds more walking. If she usually fills a small jug, should she fill a big jug? Then she adds more weight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 4. The women are allowed because there is simply no good way for them to change. He starts by showing that switching the size of the jug does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from steps 2 and 3 says to change when you can, and to act normally when you cannot. רב אשי says this case belongs in the 'cannot' group. A smaller jug means extra trips, which is more work on יום טוב. A bigger jug means a heavier load. Either way, the change adds effort instead of making the act lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: Not possible; here, no workable change exists
Walking, the trips back and forth
A load or burden being carried

phrases.english: He said to him: Because it is not possible.
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רב חנן בר רבא's question from step 4.

phrases.english: How should she act?
One who usually fills a large jug,
should she fill a small jug?
She would be increasing her walking.
One who usually fills a small jug,
should she fill a large jug?
She would be increasing her load.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by putting the women's case under the ברייתא's 'impossible to change' rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the case to the rule's built-in exception (no change is possible)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The women should be told to change how they fill and carry water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Changing the jug size only adds work, so this is a case where change is not possible.

steps.title: Covering the jug also fails, so the women may act normally
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects every way of covering the jug, because each one could lead to a new איסור. He concludes that no change is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should she cover it with a wooden lid? Sometimes it falls, and she will come to carry it by hand. Should she tie the lid on? Sometimes the rope snaps, and she will come to tie it. Should she spread a cloth over it? Sometimes it drops into the water, and she will come to squeeze it out. So, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי keeps going through other possible changes, all of them ways of covering the jug. He shows that each one could cause a problem, and he finishes by saying no change is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each covering option creates its own new problem. A lid that falls might end up carried by hand in the ordinary way. A rope that snaps might get tied again, which is קשירה. A soaked cloth might get wrung out, which is סחיטה. Since every possible change leads to trouble, the women fill their jugs the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing or wringing out liquid, which is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The women fill water normally on יום טוב because every possible change either adds work or risks a new איסור. This is exactly the 'impossible to change' case of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Should she cover it with a wooden lid?
Sometimes it falls, and she will come to carry it.
Should she tie it on?
Sometimes it snaps, and she will come to tie it.
Should she spread a cloth over it?
Sometimes it gets soaked in the water,
and she will come to squeezing it out.
Therefore, it is not possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's answer, ruling out the covering options and concluding that no change is possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering the jug might be a good way to make a change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every kind of cover risks a forbidden act, so the women may act normally.

steps.title: Why do we let women clap and dance on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנין asks אביי a question. A משנה forbids clapping, slapping the thigh and dancing on יום טוב, yet women do these things today and nobody stops them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנין said to אביי: We learned in a משנה: One may not clap, nor slap one's thigh, nor dance. But nowadays we see women doing these things, and we don't say anything to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts here, about another everyday practice that seems to break a rule. רבא בר רב חנין points out that people seem to ignore a clear משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time there is no 'it is impossible' excuse. Dancing and clapping are easy to avoid. So why is a forbidden practice going on in plain view with no one protesting?
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as the water jugs. With the jugs, there was no way to change. Here the women could easily stop, so the answer in steps 5 and 6 does not help.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנִין לְאַבָּיֵי, תְּנַן:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Chanin said to Abaye: We learned:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַפְּחִין וְאֵין מְסַפְּקִין וְאֵין מְרַקְּדִין,
phrases.english: One may not clap, nor slap the thigh, nor dance,
and nowadays we see that they do so,
and we do not say anything to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דְּקָא חָזֵינַן דְּעָבְדָן הָכִי, וְלָא אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a different practice that seems to go against the law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The common practice of letting women clap and dance on יום טוב without protest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה clearly forbids it, and there is no 'impossible to change' excuse, so the silence seems unjustified.

steps.title: אביי points to another case where no one stops the women
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a parallel case. רבא forbade sitting at the entrance of an alleyway, yet women sit there with their jugs and no one says anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And by your reasoning, what about what רבא said? A person should not sit at the entrance of an alleyway by the side post. An object might roll away from him, and he might come to carry it (four אמות in the public domain). But these women take their jugs, go and sit at the entrance of the alleyway, and we don't say anything to them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by pointing to another case with the same pattern. Women regularly break a rule set by רבא and nobody protests. He is setting up the reason for this silence, which the next step spells out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ולטעמך', אביי shows that the questioner's problem reaches beyond dancing. There is a general habit of not correcting these women. That means there must be one shared reason behind the silence. The reason itself is not given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, used to turn the question back on the asker
The side post at the entrance of an alleyway

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a well-known principle: sometimes we don't correct people who will not listen anyway. That principle is spelled out next.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רבא בר רב חנין.

phrases.english: that which Rava said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name רבא here and some don't.

phrases.english: A person should not sit at the entrance by the side post,
lest an object roll away from him
and he will come to carry it (four cubits in the public domain),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: but these women take their jugs,
and go and sit at the entrance of the alleyway,
and we do not say anything to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by showing the same silence in another case, which sets up a shared reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not stopping the dancing is a strange, one-time failure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The silence is a general pattern that must have a shared reason, which is explained next.

steps.title: Better they sin by mistake than on purpose
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his answer. We do not protest, because it is better for the people to sin without knowing than to sin knowingly. The same applies to the clapping and dancing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: leave the Jewish people alone. It is better that they sin without knowing than that they sin on purpose. Here too: leave the Jewish people alone. It is better that they sin without knowing than that they sin on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the real reason nobody stops the women. If they would not listen anyway, telling them would only turn their mistake into a deliberate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of sitting at the alleyway showed that we do sometimes stay quiet. Now אביי explains why: a rebuke that will be ignored only makes things worse. He applies the same principle to clapping and dancing on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave the Jewish people alone (do not rebuke them)
People who sin without knowing it is forbidden
People who sin on purpose, knowing it is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: When people will not listen to a rebuke, we stay silent. A sin done in ignorance is better than the same sin done knowingly.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not make clapping and dancing allowed. The act is still forbidden. The only question is whether we should protest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין, which is used across halacha when deciding whether to rebuke someone.

phrases.english: Rather: leave the Jewish people alone,
it is better that they be unwitting sinners
and not be intentional sinners.
Here too: leave the Jewish people alone,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the clapping and dancing from step 7.

phrases.english: it is better that they be unwitting sinners
and not be intentional sinners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer, which he began with the alleyway case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of not rebuking when the rebuke will be ignored
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since clapping is forbidden, we should have stopped the women.
steps.terutzMaskana: We stay silent, because a mistaken sin is better than a deliberate one.

steps.title: A suggested limit: only for rabbinic rules
steps.stepSummary: Some wanted to say that the rule of staying silent applies only to דרבנן prohibitions, not to דאורייתא ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to rabbinic prohibitions, but for Torah prohibitions it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a view that limits the rule to rabbinic prohibitions. It is setting this view up so that it can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a Torah prohibition is too serious to keep quiet about. If so, we would have to protest Torah violations even when the protest will be ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words (this rule) apply only...
A prohibition made by the Rabbis

phrases.english: And this applies only to rabbinic prohibitions,
but for Torah prohibitions — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the rule from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: the rule of staying silent covers only דרבנן prohibitions.

steps.title: No: the rule covers Torah prohibitions too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the limit. We stay silent for both Torah and rabbinic prohibitions. The proof is that people eat until dark on ערב יום כפור, even though adding time to the fast is a Torah law, and no one says anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Whether it is a Torah prohibition or a rabbinic one, we say nothing to them. For adding time to יום הכפורים is a Torah law, and yet people eat and drink until dark, and we say nothing to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא throws out the limit from step 10. It proves its point from a common Torah-level case where nobody protests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a Torah מצוה to start the fast a little before nightfall. People still eat right up to dark, and we do not rebuke them. So the rule of staying silent must apply even to Torah prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (rejecting a view)
Adding time to the start of יום כפור

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of not rebuking when people will not listen applies to Torah prohibitions as well as rabbinic ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the rule much wider. Even serious Torah violations are not protested when the protest will certainly be ignored.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
it makes no difference whether it is a Torah prohibition
or a rabbinic one,
we do not say anything at all to them,
for the adding of time to יום הכפורים
phrases.notes: Before יום כפור begins, we are supposed to start the fast a little early, while it is still day.

phrases.english: is a Torah law,
and yet they eat and drink until it gets dark,
and we do not say anything at all to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit proposed in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that the rule applies only to דרבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In practice we stay silent even about the Torah law of תוספת יום הכפורים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not rebuke for either Torah or rabbinic prohibitions when the rebuke will be ignored.

steps.title: רב כהנא: one may start taking from a storeroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which allows taking straw from a straw pile on יום טוב. רב כהנא learns from this that one may begin taking items from a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and one may begin taking from a pile of straw. רב כהנא said: this teaches that one may begin taking from a storeroom in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line of the משנה and gives רב כהנא's lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straw pile is stored away and not set aside for use on יום טוב. Even so, the משנה lets you start taking from it. So רב כהנא concludes that stored items are not off-limits, even when you are taking from them for the first time.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches (a lesson learned from a source)
In the first place, to begin with

phrases.english: And one may begin taking from a pile of straw.
רב כהנא said:
This teaches
that one may begin taking from a storeroom in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may begin taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.

steps.title: This follows רבי שמעון, who has no מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author of this ruling is. It answers רבי שמעון, because he does not hold of the prohibition of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the author of the משנה's ruling. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only someone who does not forbid מוקצה would allow taking from stored-away items. That is רבי שמעון's view, so the רישא of the משנה must be his.

keyTerms.meaning: Items set aside and not meant for use on שבת or יום טוב, so they may not be handled

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון,
who does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author behind רב כהנא's lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רישא of the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who has no מוקצה.

steps.title: But the end of the משנה sounds like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the same משנה forbids taking wood from a wood storeroom. That sounds like רבי יהודה, who does forbid מוקצה. So the משנה seems to follow two different opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: but not wood from the storeroom. Now we have come to רבי יהודה, who does hold of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 13. The end of the same משנה seems to follow the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רישא follows רבי שמעון, the סיפא should allow stored wood too. Since it forbids the wood, it seems to follow רבי יהודה. One משנה should not switch authors halfway through.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the end of the משנה
Wood stored in a storeroom that is set aside
Now we have come to (another view)

phrases.english: Look at the end of the משנה:
but not wood that is in the storeroom.
Now we have come to רבי יהודה,
who does hold of מוקצה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא forbids stored wood, which fits רבי יהודה and not רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Expensive wood: even רבי שמעון agrees
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is talking about cedar and fir wood. These are expensive, so the owner sets them aside to avoid losing money. Even רבי שמעון agrees that this kind of מוקצה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with cedar and fir wood, which is מוקצה because of fear of losing money, and even רבי שמעון agrees about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The whole משנה can still follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not forbid ordinary מוקצה. He does agree, though, about valuable items a person keeps away from because using them would cost him money. Expensive building wood is that kind of item, so the סיפא fits רבי שמעון as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedar and fir wood (expensive building wood)
Set aside because using it would cause a money loss

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי שמעון, who does not forbid ordinary מוקצה, agrees that מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבי שמעון has no מוקצה at all. This is a special kind that even he agrees to.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with cedar and fir wood,
which is מוקצה because of fear of losing money,
and even רבי שמעון agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to expensive wood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא follows רבי יהודה, so the משנה would have two different authors.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה follows רבי שמעון. The סיפא forbids only expensive wood, which is מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.

steps.title: Second version: רב כהנא's statement is on the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: Some taught רב כהנא's statement on the סיפא, which forbids taking wood from a wood storeroom. From it he learned that one may not start taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people taught רב כהנא's statement on the last part of the משנה: 'but not wood from the storage place.' רב כהנא said: this teaches that you may not begin taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רב כהנא said. In this version his statement is attached to the סיפא, and it reaches the opposite rule from the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 12), רב כהנא learned from the רישא that one may start taking from a storeroom. Here he learns from the סיפא that one may not. The second version reads the whole משנה as strict about starting to take from a storeroom.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (this statement) in a different way
The latter clause of a משנה
This is to say: a rule learned from a source
A storeroom where things are put away

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against the first version. It is a different report of what רב כהנא actually said, and it leads to the opposite rule.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the latter clause:
phrases.notes: "It" means רב כהנא's statement from Step 12.

phrases.english: but not with wood that is in the storage place.
Rav Kahana said:
This is to say,
one may not begin taking from a storeroom at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second version of רב כהנא's statement from Step 12, now based on the סיפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not begin taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.

steps.title: This version follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of this ruling as רבי יהודה, who holds that מוקצה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion fits this version and answers that it is רבי יהודה. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that one may not start taking from a storeroom means the stored items count as מוקצה. That is רבי יהודה's view, not רבי שמעון's. In the first version the author was רבי שמעון (Step 13), so here the author is reversed.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who holds of the prohibition of muktze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author of the ruling in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids מוקצה.

steps.title: But the רישא sounds like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The רישא allows starting to take from a straw pile. That seems to follow רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה, so the משנה seems split between two opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the first part of the משנה: you may begin taking from a straw pile. Now we have come to רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It points to the רישא, which is lenient about the straw pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סיפא follows רבי יהודה, the רישא should follow him too. But allowing the straw pile sounds like רבי שמעון. This is the mirror image of the קשיא in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (the opinion of)

phrases.english: Say the first clause:
one may begin taking from the pile of straw,
so we have come to Rabbi Shimon,
who does not hold of muktze!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from Step 17 that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא allows taking from a straw pile, which seems to deny מוקצה. That fits רבי שמעון, so the רישא and סיפא would follow different opinions.

steps.title: The straw is rotten
steps.stepSummary: The רישא is talking about rotten straw. Animals will not eat it, so it is ready to be used as fuel, and even רבי יהודה agrees it is not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case is rotten straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the רישא to rotten straw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rotten straw is no good as animal food, so the owner was not saving it. It stands ready for burning. That means even רבי יהודה does not call it מוקצה, and the whole משנה can follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: There, it is talking about rotten straw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא is about ordinary straw, which would make it follow רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about rotten straw, which even רבי יהודה allows. So the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Rotten straw is still good for clay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even rotten straw can be mixed into clay, so it has a use and might still be set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rotten straw? It is still fit for clay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 19. Rotten straw still has a use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the straw can be used for making clay, the owner might be saving it for that. Then it is not clearly meant for burning, and רבי יהודה might call it מוקצה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Clay or mud, used for bricks and plaster

phrases.english: Rotten straw?
But it is fit for clay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that rotten straw is not מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rotten straw can still be used for clay, so it may be set aside for that purpose and not meant for burning.

steps.title: The straw has thorns
steps.stepSummary: The straw in the משנה has thorns in it, so it cannot be used for clay. Its only use is as fuel, so it is not מוקצה even for רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is straw that has thorns in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case even more: rotten straw with thorns in it. This closes the issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thorns make the straw useless for kneading into clay. With no use left except burning, nobody sets it aside. The whole משנה now fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה. One may not start taking from a storeroom, and the straw pile is allowed only because it is rotten, thorny straw that is good only for fuel.

phrases.english: It is straw that has thorns in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rotten straw could still be used for clay, so it might be set aside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The straw has thorns, so it cannot be used for clay and is only fit for fuel. Even רבי יהודה allows it.
